front.title: Relay Storage Allowances That Expire at a Planned Contact

abstract.t: The use case and requirements document for IP in deep space asks that relays guard their buffers by authenticating and authorising the traffic sources allowed to consume buffer space, and by accounting for storage per source or traffic class. This document gives that requirement a mechanism. A storage allowance is a signed object in which a party with authority over a relay's storage states that a named holder may keep up to a stated number of octets at each named relay, until a planned contact between that relay and its next hop. A relay checks an allowance from data it already holds, without contacting the party that issued it. It charges stored data to an allowance by tagging the data in its own buffer and keeps no other state for it. No state is shared between relays, and at any instant the storage held under one allowance is no more than the sum of its rows. An allowance ends at the first contact it lists that takes place. A missed contact moves the end to the next contact listed, up to the last. The document defines the allowance, its issuance and delegation, enforcement at the relay, revocation, carriage in the Bundle Protocol and over IP, and its use with signed custody receipts for accounting.
